libraryPreparationPreflight.agent_guidance: In @BeforeAll, start the broker the same way JnatsTest.java and the mosquitto-based tests do in this repo: `new ProcessBuilder("docker", "run", "--rm", "-p", "6650:6650", "-p", "8080:8080", "apachepulsar/pulsar:4.2.5", "bin/pulsar", "standalone").inheritIO().start()`, then poll until a PulsarClient can connect before running tests, and destroy the process in @AfterAll. Connect with `PulsarClient.builder().serviceUrl("pulsar://localhost:6650").build()`. Give the readiness wait a materially longer timeout than the ~120s used for NATS/MQTT — standalone Pulsar bootstraps an embedded ZooKeeper and BookKeeper in addition to the broker, so it starts noticeably slower. No extra Maven dependency or system property is needed; pulsar-client-all already pulls in bouncycastle, opentelemetry, and jackson-annotations transitively.

deterministic_setup.reason: pulsar-client-all's connection, producer/consumer, schema, and compression (lz4/zstd/snappy) code is only reachable against a running broker; no in-process or mock broker exists. Tag matches the tested client version exactly and is published for amd64/arm64 on Docker Hub.

risks: Standalone Pulsar is heavier than the single-binary brokers already allow-listed (NATS, MQTT): it embeds ZooKeeper and BookKeeper, so container startup is slower and more memory-intensive, which could strain CI timeouts/resources relative to existing broker-client tests.
This introduces a brand-new Docker image entry (no existing pinned pulsar tag to reuse), so it needs its own allow-list addition rather than reusing a shared tag.
libraryPreparationPreflight.summary: pulsar-client-all is the full client implementation (not just API interfaces); its producer/consumer, schema, and compression code paths only execute against a live Pulsar broker, so the generated test needs a standalone Pulsar Docker container, following this repo's existing pattern for jnats/mosquitto broker clients.
